title: WhatsApp chats as court evidence - what courts actually require
p1:
A screenshot of a WhatsApp chat can look like solid proof. But can you actually win a case with just a screenshot?

Many people are surprised to learn that courts do not simply accept every chat image as unquestionable evidence.
p2:
The common belief is: “If the message is visible, it must be valid.” That is not always true.

Courts usually look at whether the chat is genuine, complete, and connected to the person who allegedly sent it. A cropped screenshot without context may raise questions about authenticity.
p3:
What makes a WhatsApp conversation stronger is proper verification of the electronic record, including details that show where it came from and that it has not been altered.

The practical lesson: save original chats, preserve the device where possible, and avoid relying only on edited screenshots. Digital conversations can become powerful evidence, but only when their reliability can be shown.
